author: The Whip Line
title: Tory austerity has driven the UK justice system to collapse
text:
Collapse of justice is a deliberate consequence of Tory austerity
It’s happening, then: years of underfunding that have led to the closures of hundreds of courts and the departure of an army of legal experts have led to the collapse of the UK justice system.
And it’s all due to austerity that was introduced for no good reason by the Tory-led government of David Cameron, back in the 2010s.
They put us on a highway to injustice.
“Last September, the backlog of trials waiting to come to Crown Court in England and Wales was 79,619 cases, double the level seen before the pandemic,” according to the BBC.
“It is on track to hit 100,000 cases by November next year and some suspects being charged with offences today are already being told their cases won’t be dealt with until 2030.
“That in turn has led to victims saying they are losing confidence in the system and walking away from the court process.
“The crisis has deep roots in cuts to spending on courts, judges and barristers. The impact of those decisions in the 2010s has been exacerbated by the pandemic, lawyers quitting criminal work over poor pay while the recruitment of extra police has led to more suspects being sent to court.”
The report goes on to say that Sir Brian Leveson, in charge of a major review of the justice system, has already called for the right to a jury trial to be scaled back and many intermediate crimes to be dealt with by a judge alone.
His second and final report has recommended 130 efficiency changes, from technical measures to allowing prison vans to use bus lanes to hit court appearance deadlines.
And he said there could not be a “pick and mix” approach to solving the problem.
This crisis is structural, long-term, and political - it was caused by politicians who deliberately decided to sabotage the justice system, and then refused to repair it.
What comes out most strongly from the BBC article is the way it tries to muddy the issues…
